- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment reverses.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is flat or rising slowly, true price often pulls back; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of sentiment are 1.00 (strong bullish), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to avoid over-optimism.
- If true price drops sharply after a high forecast, model may lag; adjust for lag by adding 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
